findings.title: Time of day transcribed without its number: 'at AM.'
findings.summary: The transcript contains a time of day with no hour, so the agent never received the actual time.

evidence.label: User transcript
evidence.value: I have a, uh, Thursday at AM. Two weeks from now. Would you like the appointment instead?

evidence.label: Agent's next reply (what it understood)
evidence.value: Thanks, but I really need to see Dr. Patel next week if possible. Could you check again for any other Tuesday morning openings?

root_cause.statement: Speech-to-text likely dropped a spoken number (for example "8" in "8 AM").
missing_evidence: Audio of the turn, or a reference transcript of what was said

next_steps: Listen to the turn to confirm what was said.
Re-run the same script with a different STT model and compare the transcript.
Add the expected times as STT keyterms, or have the agent ask for the exact time when it's missing.

findings.title: Agent said goodbye at 4:29.5 while the call was still going
findings.summary: The agent ended its side of the conversation although the other side had not wrapped up; the conversation continued afterwards.

evidence.label: User's previous turn (no closing)
evidence.value: Okay. Let's go with Thursday at AM. Two weeks from now.

evidence.label: Agent said goodbye
evidence.value: That works for me. Thank you for scheduling it. Goodbye!

evidence.label: Conversation continued
evidence.value: One moment, please. I am checking your information.

evidence.label: Agent instruction about goodbyes
evidence.value: Once your appointment is confirmed, thank them and say goodbye.

root_cause.statement: The agent may have inferred that the conversation was complete and triggered its closing behavior too early. Its instructions mention saying goodbye and may have contributed.
missing_evidence: A re-run of the same script with the goodbye instruction rewritten

next_steps: Instruct the agent to say goodbye only after the other side wraps up.
Re-run the same script and check that the goodbye moves to the end.

findings.title: 1 of 35 user turns ended by the 2.5s endpointing timeout
findings.summary: For these turns the turn detector never judged the user finished, so the agent waited the full 2.5s before replying.

evidence.label: End-of-turn delay at 3:53.8
evidence.value: 2.5s: "There is no opening next week. I'm sorry."

evidence.label: Agent response latency after these turns

root_cause.statement: The user paused or trailed off mid-thought, so end-of-turn prediction stayed uncertain until the maximum delay.

next_steps: Read the timed-out turns: are they fragments or complete sentences?
If complete, check turn-detector settings; if fragments, the wait was correct.
Avoid lowering max_endpointing_delay blindly: it would cut users off mid-sentence.
